infos.name: PWM_CONTROLLER
infos.comment: Configures the CPU internal PWM peripheral to generate a PWM signal through hardware. If the CPU does not have a PWM peripheral, compiling this block will result in a compilation error. CHANNEL is the PWM channel number. For most Arduino boards that number is the pin number for the PWM capable pin. FREQ is the desired PWM frequency in Hz. DUTY is the PWM duty cycle (between 0 and 100).

infos.name: TCP_CONNECT
infos.comment: Connect to a remote TCP server when CONNECT is TRUE. Upon success, this block returns the connection ID on SOCKET_ID. If SOCKET_ID is less than zero, then the connection was not successfull

infos.name: TCP_SEND
infos.comment: Send a message to a remote device using TCP/IP when SEND is TRUE. SOCKET_ID must receive a connection ID from a successfull connection using the TCP_Connect block. BYTES_SENT returns the number of bytes sent to the remote device. If BYTES_SENT is less than zero then an error occurred while trying to send the message

infos.name: TCP_RECEIVE
infos.comment: Send a message to a remote device using TCP/IP when SEND is TRUE. SOCKET_ID must receive a connection ID from a successfull connection using the TCP_Connect block. BYTES_RECEIVED returns the number of bytes received from the remote device. MSG is a String containing the message received

infos.name: TCP_CLOSE
infos.comment: Close the TCP connection with the remote server. If SUCCESS is less than zero, then the connection was not successfully closed, or the connection does not exist anymore.

infos.name: MQTT_RECEIVE
infos.comment: Receive MQTT messages for a particular TOPIC when RECEIVE is active. You must subscribe to a topic first before you can start receiving messages for that particular topic. Once a message is received, RECEIVED output is triggered, and MESSAGE will contain the received message as a STRING.

infos.name: MQTT_SEND
infos.comment: Sends a MESSAGE to a particular TOPIC when SEND input is triggered. Keep in mind that SEND is not configured as a rising edge input, which means that MQTT_SEND will continuously send messages every scan cycle while SEND is TRUE. If the message was sent without errors, SUCCESS will be TRUE.

infos.name: MQTT_CONNECT
infos.comment: Connect to a BROKER at a given PORT when CONNECT is triggered. If a successfull connection is made, SUCCESS is set to TRUE

infos.name: MQTT_CONNECT_AUTH
infos.comment: Connect to an authenticated BROKER at a given PORT using the credentials from USER and PASSWORD when CONNECT is triggered. If a successfull connection is made, SUCCESS is set to TRUE

infos.name: MQTT_SUBSCRIBE
infos.comment: Subscribe to a given TOPIC when SUBSCRIBE input is triggered. Upon a successfull subscription, SUCCESS is set to TRUE. Keep in mind that once you subscribe to a topic, OpenPLC will start receiving messages sent to that topic and storing them in a message pool. You must use the MQTT_RECEIVE block to retrieve messages from the pool and free up space to receive more messages. The maximum pool size is currently limited to 10 messages. If you let messages accumulate in the pool you will start loosing messages once the pool is full.

infos.name: MQTT_UNSUBSCRIBE
infos.comment: Unsubscribe to a given TOPIC when UNSUBSCRIBE input is triggered. Upon a successfull unsubscription, SUCCESS is set to TRUE. Keep in mind that once you unsubscribe to a topic, OpenPLC will stop storing messages sent to that topic in the message pool. However, messages received previously and not captured with a MQTT_RECEIVE block will remain in the pool using up pool space.

infos.name: MQTT_DISCONNECT
infos.comment: Disconnects from the current broker when DISCONNECT is set to TRUE. Upon a successfull disconnection, SUCCESS is set to TRUE.
